title: Micro wins & checkpoints — merge log
body:
Purpose: quick personal notebook to capture tiny, high-leverage steps that make refactors/PRs safe to land (and cheap to revert).

Why this exists:
- I keep making the same mental tradeoffs when slicing refactors and forgetting small automation hooks that would save future reviewers hours.
- Aim: capture micro-wins, guarded rollouts, and quick test ideas I can reuse across repos.

Quick checklist (pre-merge, < 15 min audit):
- ✅ README/PR description: include intent, how rollback will work (branch + revert command).
- ✅ Small surface tests added for changed contract (not full e2e). Prefer property-based or targeted unit where cheap.
- ✅ Toggle/feature flag? Add a quick default-off flag and a rollout note.
- ✅ Metrics: add one counter and one latency gauge (if touching hot path) and wire to debug log initially.
- ✅ Post-merge canary plan: percentage/time window + owner.
- ✅ Link to infra tickets / deployment playbook in PR.

Tiny safety patterns I keep forgetting:
- 'noop' DB migration pattern: new column added as nullable, backfill separate PR, then non-null in later PR.
- Schema-change ephemeral flag: when changing payload shape, include backward-compatible parsing path and a short test showing both old & new payloads accepted.
- Quick kill switch: env var that flips to old code path when set; document name and location in PR body.

Mini-test ideas (cheap, high-signal):
- Randomized small-input fuzz for parser edgecases (100 samples in CI, not flakey).
- Deterministic null/empty value permutations around boundary logic.
- Golden micro-snapshots for serialization format (strip timestamps).

Merge-time commands (copyable):
- Local smoke: 
  ./scripts/run-small-smoke.sh --pr 8421
- Revert flow: 
  git checkout main && git pull && git revert -m 1 <merge-commit> && git push origin main && open PR
- Quick canary deploy (k8s): 
  kubectl apply -f k8s/canary-v1.yaml && kubectl rollout status deployment/serving-runtime-canary

Rollout notes template (paste into PR body):
- Canary window: 30m at 5% traffic -> 2h at 25% -> 100% if stable.
- Owner: @<oncall> (first 2h), @team (next 24h).
- Metrics to watch: error-rate (alerts on +0.5%), median latency p50/p95, token-cost-per-request.
- Revert plan: immediate revert + block rollout if alert fires twice in window.

Small refactor heuristics (how to keep size small):
- Cut PR into: (A) API contract + tests, (B) implementation change, (C) optimization. Merge A first.
- If touching hot path, do functional correctness first; perf follow-up in separate PR with benchmark.
- When renaming, prefer aliasing + follow-up cleanup to avoid long churn in history.

Post-merge follow-ups (within 24–72h):
- Add a one-line comment in the team slack channel summarizing the outcome (include metrics link).
- If revert happened: quick blameless timeline and note saved under confluence + link from PR.
- Add a small TODO in code for the tech debt created (e.g., // TODO: remove legacy-flag after 2025-01).

Unresolved questions I keep returning to:
- How much test coverage is 'enough' for small runtime changes that touch batching logic? (50% of changed functions? specific edge cases?)
- Should we standardize a single canary window template across services or keep service-specific?

Sample short PR body (boilerplate):
Title: [serving-runtime] keep kv-cache stable during partial refactor
Body:
- What: small change to eviction heuristic to avoid double-free when cache-map and backend disagree.
- Why: observed flake in integration that correlated to eviction race.
- Safety: added targeted unit to reproduce race and a canary rollout (5% -> 25% -> 100%).
- Rollout plan: (see rollout section above)
- Revert: git revert <merge-commit> + canary rollback command.
- Linked artifacts: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/8421, JIRA INF-2193

Personal TODO (short):
- [ ] Write a small script that auto-inserts rollout template into PR body from a YAML snippet.
- [ ] Add a one-liner into PR template reminding to add revert instructions.
- [ ] Try 100-run randomized parser fuzz in CI for a week and review flakiness.

Notes to self (less polished):
- Stop trying to do both correctness + perf in same PR unless it's trivial.
- Use canary flag naming pattern: repo.service.feature.<short>. Example: serving.kv.eviction.v2
- Keep canary windows documented as comments in deployment manifests so infra folks don't have to hunt the PR.

Random links I referenced:
- Confluence merge safety guidelines (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/merge-safety-guidelines
- PR that caused the recent eviction flake (for context): https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/8421
- Jira ticket I keep meaning to revisit: INF-2193

End.
